I've been farming this land for 30 years now. I'm 52, got my middle school certificate, and I know these fields pretty well. Got 10.1 mu total — about 7 mu I keep in wheat-maize double crop, that's my main food and income. The other 3.1 mu I'm putting in potato this spring. Seven people in the house, but two of my sons work off-farm in Shijiazhuang, so it's mostly me, my wife, and my old man for daily work. We hire help when the harvest gets tight.

**The wheat** is already in the ground from last October. I used the improved variety, about 12.5 kg seed per mu, cost around 35 yuan per mu with the seed treatment. Before planting I put down 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu as base. Now it's March, and I'm thinking about spring. The extension station says 15–18 kg nitrogen per mu is enough, but I've seen years where that wasn't quite right, so I usually do a bit more to be safe — I'll topdress 20 kg of urea per mu at jointing, probably late March when the wheat starts turning green strong. That puts my total nitrogen around 17 kg per mu, plus about 7 kg each of phosphorus and potassium from the compound. I'll irrigate three times if it's dry — once at green-up, once right after the topdressing so the fertilizer gets in, and once at heading. Pumping costs money, about 15–20 yuan each time, so if we get decent rain I might skip the green-up one. For pesticides, I'll spray herbicide if I see weeds coming, and maybe fungicide if powdery mildew shows up like it did two years ago. I'm expecting about 450 kg per mu if the weather holds.

**The potato** on the 3.1 mu — I'll plant late March. I saved about half my seed potatoes from last year, bought the rest, so seed cost me about 150 yuan per mu for what I purchased. Potato needs more fertilizer, especially potassium. I'll put about 80 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, and I add extra potassium because tubers need it. I'll topdress once when the tubers start forming. Total nitrogen about 12 kg per mu, phosphorus 8 kg, potassium around 16 kg. I'll irrigate three times — at planting, flowering, and when the tubers are swelling. Potato is heavy on labor, lots of hilling and checking, so that's maybe 18 family days and I'll hire 4 days of help. Hoping for around 1,600 kg per mu.

**Then June comes** — the crazy week. I harvest the wheat and need to get the maize in fast, sometimes only five or six days. I hire a combine for wheat, it's 50 yuan per mu but saves us days. For the maize I use hybrid seed, about 3 kg per mu at roughly 55 yuan. I put compound fertilizer in the furrow at planting, about 50 kg per mu, then topdress with urea at jointing — say 15 kg. Total nitrogen around 16 kg per mu. I'll irrigate twice, maybe three times if July is scorching. Weed control is mainly herbicide at planting. Maize doesn't need as much daily tending, maybe 12 family days and 2 hired days for planting and harvest. I'm expecting about 500 kg per mu.

**Money-wise**, I'm careful. Total input cost — seed, fertilizer, pesticide, irrigation, hired labor — I'm looking at about 6,800 yuan this year. That's a big chunk of cash, and my wife worries when we spend that much up front. But I remember my neighbor tried to save on fertilizer three years ago and lost almost 100 kg per mu on his wheat. Better to spend a bit more and not lose sleep. Still, I'm not made of money — every yuan has to count.
